channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President to Visit South Korea for State Visit September 13-16
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will undertake a state visit to South Korea from September 13-16 at the invitation of President Lee Jae-myung. Discussions will focus on strengthening strategic partnership, deepening cooperation, and cultural exchanges. Mirziyoyev will also attend the first Central Asia-South Korea summit.

item.title: Iran Used Chinese Satellite Images for Attack on US Base in Jordan
item.description: Iran reportedly used Chinese satellite imagery to plan an attack on a US base in Jordan, which damaged over 20 structures and killed three people. Washington considers this strong evidence of Chinese support for attacks resulting in American military casualties.

item.title: Uzbekistan Condemns Attacks on Saudi Arabia, Urges Diplomatic Resolution
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed deep concern over missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. The ministry strongly condemns any actions threatening civilian infrastructure, regional security, and international navigation. Uzbekistan supports UN and regional efforts to de-escalate tensions and establish lasting peace through political and diplomatic means.

item.title: Court Financing to Be Solely from State Budget, Distribution Rules Set
item.description: Financing for court activities will exclusively come from the state budget. The Constitutional Court, Supreme Court, and Supreme Judicial Council will distribute allocated funds themselves. For other courts, fund distribution will be managed by the Department for Ensuring Court Activities under the Supreme Court.

item.title: Parliaments of Uzbekistan and Lithuania to support mutually beneficial initiatives
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis visited Lithuania for meetings with parliamentary groups on cooperation. Discussions focused on inter-parliamentary interaction, legislative improvement, regional development, environmental protection, and water resource management. Both sides agreed to strengthen cooperation and support mutually beneficial initiatives.

item.title: Uzbek President to Visit South Korea for First Central Asia-Korea Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will undertake a state visit to South Korea to attend the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit. Discussions will focus on cooperation in trade, investment, infrastructure, digital transformation, science, and technology.

item.title: Uzbekistan's National Bank plans to issue $250 million in bonds on Chinese capital market
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Bank for Foreign Economic Activity (UzSberbank) has agreed to cooperate with China International Capital Corporation (CICC) on the Asian capital market. The bank plans to issue international bonds worth $250 million in Hong Kong, marking its debut on the Asian debt market.

item.title: Uzbekistan Condemns Missile and Drone Attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Uzbekistan has strongly condemned missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that any actions threatening the safety of regional states, civilian and energy infrastructure, and international shipping are unacceptable. The ministry emphasized its stance against the use of force against civilian populations.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Visit South Korea on State Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will undertake a state visit to South Korea from September 13-16 at the invitation of President Lee Jae-myung. Discussions will focus on strengthening strategic partnership, deepening cooperation in priority areas, and enhancing cultural-humanitarian exchanges. Mirziyoyev will also attend the first Central Asia-South Korea summit.

item.title: Woman and Child Die After Falling From 15th Floor in Astana
item.description: A 27-year-old woman and a two-year-old child have died in Astana after the woman fell from a 15th-floor apartment window onto a stroller. The child, who was in the stroller, also died from injuries sustained in the incident. Police have opened a criminal investigation into the circumstances.

item.title: Kazakhstan to host AI MONTH 2026, integrating key AI events into a tech program
item.description: Kazakhstan launches AI MONTH 2026, a comprehensive artificial intelligence and digital technology program starting September 23. The initiative unites the tech community, business, education, startups, and international experts. The central event is the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum in Astana, October 1-3, featuring HackAlem AI powered by OpenAI.

item.title: Tajikistan's Irrigation System Faces Hundreds of Millions in Debt
item.description: Tajikistan's irrigation system is burdened by hundreds of millions in debt. The article explores the current state of the system and the reasons behind its significant financial challenges, questioning the sustainability of its operations.

item.title: Top Prosecutors of Tajikistan and Iran Discuss Cooperation in Kazakhstan
item.description: The Prosecutor Generals of Tajikistan and Iran met in Kazakhstan to discuss strengthening professional cooperation and combating global threats like extremism and drug trafficking. They also addressed the situation in the Middle East and the extradition of convicted individuals.

item.title: Putin Proposes BRICS Payment System and Grain Exchange
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed to BRICS the creation of a common payment infrastructure, investment platform, reinsurance mechanism, and grain exchange. He also advocated for increased representation of Asian, African, and Latin American countries in the UN Security Council and reform of global financial institutions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President opens new bean processing plant in Talas region
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov inaugurated a bean processing plant in Kyrgyzstan's Talas region, part of a national launch of 60 industrial facilities. The plant, with an investment of 200 million soms, has a capacity of 40,000 tonnes annually and created 100 jobs.

item.title: Uzbek President orders development of commercial complexes in Tashkent districts
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has ordered the preparation of a four-year program to improve 400 neighborhoods in Tashkent, allocating 10 trillion soms. He instructed district governors to establish two major commercial complexes in each district to attract visitors.

item.title: Tajikistan seeks to increase fuel purchases from abroad
item.description: Tajikistan intends to increase its purchases of petroleum products from abroad. The country may require more imported petroleum products in the coming years, despite efforts to diversify supply sources.

item.title: Earthquake in Kyrgyzstan felt in Uzbekistan's Andijan and Namangan regions
item.description: An earthquake that occurred in Kyrgyzstan was felt in Uzbekistan. The tremors registered with a magnitude of 2 in the Andijan and Namangan regions of Uzbekistan.

item.title: Jyrgalan ski resort to open December 1, says Kyrgyzstan President Japarov
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Jyrgalan ski resort will open on December 1, announced President Sadyr Japarov. The first phase of the Ala-Too Resort ski cluster is complete, aiming to boost tourism and create jobs. Further infrastructure development is planned through 2026.

item.title: Bukhara governor promises to eliminate poverty and unemployment by year-end
item.description: Bukhara Governor Botir Zaripov has pledged to completely eradicate poverty and unemployment in the region by the end of the year. Since the beginning of the year, poverty and unemployment have decreased by 2 percent, and over 10,000 vacant jobs are currently available.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP claims organized crime blocked binary options ban
item.description: Member of Parliament Dastan Bekeshev stated that his bill to ban binary options was blocked from passing the second reading due to the influence of organized crime groups on lawmakers. He believes the current bill, initiated by the Cabinet of Ministers, needs stronger enforcement, including identifying bank accounts and crypto wallets.

item.title: Uzbekistan Minister: Shortcomings Remain in Applying Student Knowledge Scientifically
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Preschool and School Education, Hilola Karimova, stated that while PISA 2025 results show progress, challenges persist. The ministry will focus on improving students' ability to apply their knowledge in scientific contexts, identifying this as a key task for the education system.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Imposes Six-Month Ban on Livestock Exports to Ensure Food Security
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has implemented a temporary six-month ban on the export of cattle, horses, sheep, and goats to safeguard food security and stabilize prices. Exceptions include transit animals, sport horses, gifted horses, breeding sheep, and livestock not raised domestically.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor Reports Full Disbursement of 'Bala Yrysy' Program Funds
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor, Social Security, and Migration has disbursed 285.5 million soms to 232,229 recipients under the 'Bala Yrysy' state program as of September 10, 2026. The ministry is working with banks to resolve any discrepancies in fund reception.

item.title: Tashkent to Implement New Procedures for Resolving Investor Issues
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced new procedures for addressing investor concerns in Tashkent. The president criticized districts lagging in investment attraction and outlined plans to specialize city districts by economic focus, aiming to attract $9 billion in investments by 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan medical staff appeal to president over jailed doctor
item.description: Staff at the National Center for Maternity and Child Welfare have appealed to President Sadyr Japarov regarding the case of nephrologist Nasira Beishebaeva. A Bishkek court sentenced her to three years in prison and ordered compensation for a patient's adverse outcome. The medical staff argue that the outcome was not intentional and fear that doctors will be afraid to work.

item.title: Earthquake in Kyrgyzstan Felt in Andijan and Namangan Regions of Uzbekistan
item.description: An earthquake originating in Kyrgyzstan on September 12 was felt in Uzbekistan's Andijan and Namangan regions. The tremor had a magnitude of 3.9 in Jalal-Abad, Kyrgyzstan, at a depth of 16 kilometers. Felt intensity in Uzbekistan was rated at 2 points.

item.title: Hydrogen Storage to Stabilize Autonomous Power Systems Within Seconds After Failures
item.description: Tomsk Polytechnic University scientists and Chinese researchers have developed a model for an autonomous power system using hydrogen storage. This system can quickly restore power stability after accidents or load changes, making it valuable for remote locations and industrial sites relying on renewable energy sources.

item.title: US Invites Russia to G20 Energy Ministers Meeting in Texas
item.description: The United States has invited Russia to participate in the G20 Energy Ministers meeting scheduled for September 14-16 in Texas. A White House representative confirmed a Russian official would attend the Houston summit, though the specific individual has not yet been identified.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President inaugurates bean processing plant in Talas region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov opened a bean processing plant in the Talas region, investing 200 million soms. The facility has a capacity of 40,000 tons annually and created 100 jobs. The president highlighted the region's agricultural potential and the importance of domestic processing for economic growth.

item.title: Labor migrants contributed nearly $4 billion to Russia's budget in six months
item.description: Labor migrants contributed approximately $4 billion to Russia's budget in the first half of the year. This amount represents a 30% increase compared to the same period last year. The data highlights the significant financial impact of migrant labor on the Russian economy.

item.title: Saudi Arabia's main oil pipeline bypassing Hormuz halted after drone attack
item.description: Saudi Arabia's main oil pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, has been halted following a drone attack. The 1,200-kilometer pipeline transported 4-5 million barrels of oil daily in recent months, accounting for 4-5% of global oil supply. The incident raises concerns about regional energy security.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan scientific organizations to set prices for their own developments
item.description: State scientific and scientific-technical organizations in Kyrgyzstan will be able to set their own prices for the results of their research and development. The Cabinet of Ministers chairman signed a corresponding resolution. The document clarifies the right of these organizations to earn income from research, educational, consulting, publishing, and commercial activities. Changes were also made to the National Academy of Sciences charter regarding tariffs for paid services.

item.title: First South Korea-Central Asia Summit to be held in Seoul
item.description: The first summit between South Korea and the leaders of five Central Asian nations—Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan—will take place in Seoul on September 16, 2026. South Korean President Lee Jae-myung will hold separate bilateral talks with the leaders on September 14-16. Key topics include expanding trade and investment, energy cooperation, critical minerals, and supply chains.

item.title: Medical union supports convicted nephrologist Nasira Beyshebaeva
item.description: The Central Committee of the Healthcare Workers' Union of Kyrgyzstan has expressed support for nephrologist Nasira Beyshebaeva, stating readiness to protect her rights. The union acknowledged the family's grief and the tragic nature of the event but urged consideration of the medical profession's specifics and the circumstances of medical decisions. Beyshebaeva was sentenced to three years in prison for alleged medical error.

item.title: Museum complex dedicated to writer Chinghiz Aitmatov opens in his native village
item.description: The 'Aitmatov Aalamy' cultural and memorial complex has opened in Sheker, Talas region, the birthplace of writer Chinghiz Aitmatov. President Sadyr Japarov attended the ceremony. The complex aims to be a center for education, science, and culture, promoting the writer's legacy for younger generations and contributing to a 'Kyrgyz Renaissance'.

item.title: Social media videos checked for inciting inter-ethnic hatred in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Police in Suzak district are investigating an Instagram post suspected of inciting inter-ethnic hatred. The video was found on September 9 during an online monitoring. An examination has been ordered, and a legal assessment will be made after the investigation concludes. The publication belongs to a citizen identified as M.M.

item.title: Tajik Prosecutor General Attends ECO Meeting on Combating Transnational and Cybercrime
item.description: Tajikistan's Prosecutor General, Habibullo Vohidzoda, participated in the seventh meeting of ECO Prosecutors General in Turkestan, Kazakhstan. Delegates from Azerbaijan, Iran, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan discussed digitalization of criminal prosecution, combating cybercrime, internet fraud, cryptocurrency crimes, and the shadow economy.

item.title: Organized crime groups allegedly blocked ban on binary options in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan MP Dastan Bekeshev stated that organized crime groups influenced lawmakers, preventing a ban on binary options after its first reading. He supports a new government-initiated bill but believes its enforcement mechanism needs refinement, particularly regarding identifying financial accounts.

item.title: Korea-Central Asia Summit Elevates Partnership to Strategic Level
item.description: The first Korea-Central Asia summit marks a significant upgrade in the partnership, moving from inter-agency coordination to strategic decision-making. This elevation coincides with Uzbek President Mirziyoyev's state visit to South Korea, signaling Seoul's view of Central Asia as a key strategic partner and reflecting regional transformation.
